claims: The CDC recommends an annual flu shot for everyone 6 months and older.
The CDC recommends getting the flu shot ideally by the end of October.
Flu shot protection takes about two weeks to develop.
The CDC advises getting the flu vaccine by the end of October.
Getting vaccinated against flu later, even in January or beyond, is still beneficial as long as the virus is circulating.
Annual vaccination is recommended for everyone aged 6 months and older.
Seniors aged 65+ are individuals at higher risk of flu complications.
Young children are individuals at higher risk of flu complications.
Pregnant women are individuals at higher risk of flu complications.
People with chronic diseases such as asthma and diabetes are individuals at higher risk of flu complications.
The flu vaccine is designed to protect against the three or four influenza viruses likely to circulate each season.
Studies show the flu vaccine can reduce the severity of illness even if a person gets the flu.
Studies show the flu vaccine can reduce the risk of hospitalization even if a person gets the flu.
Most flu vaccines are administered via needle.
Some flu vaccine options are available for individuals aged 18-64 via jet injector.
Flu vaccines cannot cause the flu.
Flu shots can be given at the same time as a COVID-19 vaccine.
Flu shots are generally covered at no cost by Medicare Part B.
Flu shots are generally covered at no cost by most private insurance plans.
Flu shots are available at pharmacies such as CVS and Walmart.
Flu shots are available at doctor's offices.
Flu shots are available at health clinics.
Flu shots are sometimes available at workplaces or schools
